newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EURO POWERS KEEP WORLD CUP FINALS IN VIEW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EURO POWERS KEEP WORLD CUP FINALS IN VIEW.

text.p: Four of European soccer's major powers -- Germany, Italy, Holland and England -- all collected wins on Wednesday to keep alive their very real hopes of reaching next year's World Cup finals in France.

The only one of Europe's big five not to win on a busy night of 19 qualifying matches around the continent were Spain, who were held to a 1-1 draw by a Yugoslavia side, fast regaining their former prowess, in Belgrade.
European champions Germany claimed an important 2-0 group nine victory over Ukraine with second half goals by Oliver Bierhoff and Mario Basler.
Germany are now just a point behind Ukraine and two clear of Portugal.
Italy stayed four points ahead of England in group two with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Poland.
Roberto Di Matteo, Paolo Maldini and the recalled Roberto Baggio with a brilliant solo were on target in Naples to take the 1994 World Cup runners-up to 16 points from six games.

England stayed on their tail on 12 points -- and a match in hand -- but made hard work of beating Georgia 2-0 at Wembley. Teddy Sheringham's first half header proved decisive in a far from impressive showing. Alan Shearer blasted home the second with the final kick of the game after Sheringham laid a freekick back into his path following a Georgia backpass to the goalkeeper.

Holland thrashed San Marino 6-0 to stay in control of group seven. Two goals by Dennis Bergkamp and one each for Aron Winter, Pierre van Hooijdonk, Frank de Boer and John Bosman moved Holland to 15 points -- three clear of Belgium.
The Belgians earned a vital 3-1 win in Turkey thanks to a first-half hat-trick by Luis Olivera. Oktay Derelioglu replied for the Turks, also in the first half.
Romania all but ensured their place in next year's finals in France with a 1-0 home win over Ireland in group eight.
Adrian Ilie got the only goal after 32 minutes but keeper Bogdan Stelea saved a Roy Keane penalty three minutes after the break.
Romania have a maximum 18 points from six games, eight clear of Macedonia with Ireland down to fourth on seven points.
Elsewhere in group eight Lithuania beat Liechtenstein 2-0 away to stay in the hunt in third place on nine points
Scotland conceded their first goals in seven qualifying matches when Sweden won their group four clash 2-1 in Gothenburg.
Kennet Andersson volleyed Sweden into a deserved lead two minutes before half-time and added the second in the 63rd minute.
Scotland, who replied through Kevin Gallacher late on, still top the group on 14 points with Austria, who beat Estonia 2-0, second on 10 and Sweden third on nine.
Spain's traditional charge to early qualification slowed slightly as they drew 1-1 in Yugolsavia.
Fernando Hierro's 19th minute penalty looked to have given Spain victory only for Predrag Mijatovic to equalise with another spot kick three minutes from time.
Spain top group six with 17 points, one clear of Yugoslavia.
Group one was blown open as leaders Greece lost 1-0 at home to Croatia and Denmark thrashed Slovenia 4-0.
Two goals by Allan Nielsen and one each for Per Pedersen and Brian Laudrup had Denmark's result settled within an hour and sent the 1992 European champions to the top of the group on 10 points.
Greece trail on goal difference, with Croatia third on nine points thanks to Davor Suker's 74th minute winner in Salonika.
Group three leaders Norway were held 1-1 at home by Finland -- their first dropped points in four games.
They still top the standings on 10 points with Switzerland and Hungary both on six. The Swiss beat Hungary 1-0 in Zurich with a late goal by Kubilay Turkyilmaz.
Israel stayed in contention to reach the finals for the first time since 1970 with a 2-0 home win over Cyprus -- both goals coming from veteran striker Eli Ohana.
The win keeps Israel top of group five with 13 points from six games with Russia second on 11 from five.
The Russians had a comfortable 3-0 win over Luxembourg in Moscow with goals by Valery Kechinov, Sergei Grishin and Igor Simutenkov.

Elsewhere a last minute goal by Tody Jonsson gave the Faroe Islands a 2-1 win in Malta in group six -- their first ever World Cup victory, two goals by Juri Shevlyakov earned Latvia a 2-0 home win over Belarus in group four and Armenia and Northern Ireland drew 0-0 in group nine.
